numberItems.stem: On the skills tests, which language offense on the same test date ends the test as an automatic failure?
numberItems.explanation: The first 2 offenses on the same date get verbal warnings; the 3rd ends the test as an automatic failure (p. 11-1).

numberItems.stem: How many attempts do you get to pass the three skills tests?
options: 3 for each of the three tests
3 in total for all three tests
numberItems.explanation: You get 3 tries in all to pass the vehicle inspection, basic control skills and road test (p. 11-1).

numberItems.stem: On the in-cab check, you build air to governor cut-out. About what pressure is that?
numberItems.explanation: Governor cut-out is about 120–140 psi, or the maker's figure (p. 11-3).

numberItems.stem: Instead of 3 red reflective triangles, which warning devices may you carry?
options: Tire chains and a tool kit
numberItems.explanation: Required warning devices are 3 red reflective triangles, 6 fuses, or 3 liquid-burning flares; tire chains are optional (p. 11-3).

numberItems.stem: How do you do the hydraulic brake check in the cab?
options: Pump the pedal 5 times, then hold it 3 seconds
Pump the pedal 3 times, then hold it 5 seconds
Pump the pedal 3 times, then hold it 1 minute
numberItems.explanation: Pump 3 times, then hold 5 seconds; the pedal must not sink (p. 11-4).

numberItems.stem: In the Hydro-Boost check, how much pedal force do you hold while starting the engine?
numberItems.explanation: Hold the pedal with light pressure, 15–25 pounds, and start the engine; it should give a little and then hold (p. 11-4).

numberItems.stem: In the 1-minute applied leakage test, what is the most air a single vehicle may lose?
numberItems.explanation: The limit is 3 psi for a single vehicle, 4 psi for a combination of 2 and 6 psi for 3 or more (p. 5-8).

numberItems.stem: In the spring brake test, the parking brake knob normally pops out at about:
numberItems.explanation: As you fan the air down, the parking brake knob should pop out, normally at 20–45 psi (p. 5-9).

numberItems.stem: A vehicle is out of service when how many of its leaf springs are missing or broken?
numberItems.explanation: When 1/4 or more of the leaves are missing or broken, the vehicle is out of service (p. 11-5).

numberItems.stem: With the brakes released, how far may a manual slack adjuster's pushrod move when you pull it by hand?
numberItems.explanation: On manual slack adjusters, the pushrod should not move more than 1 inch by hand with the brakes released (p. 11-5).

numberItems.stem: What is the minimum tread depth on tires that are NOT on the steering axle?
numberItems.explanation: Steering-axle tires need 4/32 inch; all other tires need at least 2/32 inch (p. 11-6).

numberItems.stem: How full must the DEF tank be on a truck with after-treatment?
numberItems.explanation: The DEF tank must be more than 1/8 full and the DEF dash indicator must work (p. 11-7).

numberItems.stem: On a bus inspection, how many emergency exits must you demonstrate?
options: At least 1, and describe the rest
numberItems.explanation: Demonstrate at least 1 emergency exit, then point out and describe all the others (pp. 11-9, 11-11).

numberItems.stem: For a Class B or C test, how is the vehicle inspection version chosen?
options: You get 1 of 3 versions, learned just before the test
You choose the version in advance
numberItems.explanation: Class B and C get 1 of 3 equal versions and learn which just before the test; 1 of 4 is for Class A (p. 11-11).
